title: Revise eval scoring and judge calibration for config- and model-change regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current eval scoring mixes raw LLM-judge outputs and ad-hoc rubrics. When model or serving config changes (quantization, kernels, batching), we see noisy score shifts that generate false positives or miss real regressions. Goals: 1) Define a stable rubric and score aggregation that is robust to distributional drift caused by infra/config changes. 2) Calibrate LLM-as-judge scores against a gold set and uncertainty estimates so alerts have actionable precision. 3) Integrate statistical significance and effect-size checks into regression alerts and CI gates. 4) Surface per-workload baselines and per-customer sensitivity in Console alerts and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical rubric doc published and reviewed by Research/Applied ML and Eng: scoring dimensions, example annotations, and edge-case rules
LLM-as-judge calibration run completed: mapping raw judge scores -> calibrated probabilities + confidence intervals for 3 judge models (gpt-judge-large, redwood-judge-v1, open-judge-2)
New composite scoring function implemented in evals pipeline with weighted metrics, and documented default weights
Regression alerting logic updated to require: (a) effect size > min_delta AND (b) p-value < 0.01 using bootstrap on judge votes OR Bayesian credible interval exclusion
Integration tests and a canary pipeline that gates model/config rollouts using the new scoring; CI will block deployment on high-impact regressions
Console dashboard: new per-route evaluation card and historical calibration visualization available in staging
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (1 week): Draft rubric with examples and failure modes; collect 500 gold judgments across core workloads (chat, summarization, reranking)
Phase 2 (1 week): Calibrate LLM-as-judge scores. Use temperature sweeps and label smoothing; produce reliability diagrams and Brier scores for each judge model
Phase 3 (1 week): Implement composite scorer in evals service (pluggable scoring module) + significance tests (bootstrap + Bayesian option)
Phase 4 (1 week): Wire alerts into Console and CI canary. Add per-customer baseline storage and decay policy for historical baselines
Phase 5 (ongoing): Monitor false positive/negative rate for 4 weeks, iterate weights and threshold; document rollback playbook and two test incidents
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose to keep LLM-as-judge as primary signal but require calibration and an orthogonal automated metric (token-level overlap or semantic-similarity) to reduce single-source bias — agreed by research and eng
2026-03-12: Adopted bootstrap + effect-size threshold as primary regression test; Bayesian credible intervals will be supported for customers that prefer probabilistic alerts
2026-03-13: Decided default composite weights: 50% calibrated judge score, 30% semantic-similarity, 20% task-specific metric (e.g., ROUGE for summarization); weights configurable per-workload
